newsitem.title: UK: EMI squeezed higher in stock shortage.
newsitem.headline: EMI squeezed higher in stock shortage.

text.p: Shares in EMI Group Plc rose in early trading on Tuesday, recovering from recent sharp losses and squeezed higher amid a shortage of stock in the market, dealers said.
"There is no particular story today, it's just that they were never that bad in the first place," said one market-maker in the stock.
Extending a rebound from the 18-month low of 10.95 stg set earlier this month, the stock was up 24p at 12.32-1/2 stg by 0834 GMT in thin volume of just 16,950 shares.
"The fall they had was all down to one "sell" note which caused some panic to get out," the market-maker said. "Now we're seeing the same thing on the upside."
Added another market-maker: "The stock is very squeezy, there have been some big bear positions out there for some time."
Shares in EMI tumbled earlier this month as analysts at Schroders began coverage of the stock with an "underperform" rating, saying it should be sold down to 10.00 stg.

In recent months the stock has also been weighed down by worries over the state of the music market in the UK and United States. EMI is due to issue its next quarterly results statement on February 25.
